summary.text: King of the Lapiths at Larissa, son of Ixion in the genealogies, who married Hippodameia and drove the shaggy centaurs from Mount Pelium — and later bound himself with Theseus to marry daughters of Zeus, a vow that took both heroes to the house of Hades.

story.text: Homer remembers him twice over: Zeus loved the wife of Ixion and she bore Peirithous, peer of the gods in counsel; and in the Catalogue the Lapith Polypoetes is son of Peirithous, whom immortal Zeus begat — born on the day Peirithous got vengeance on the shaggy centaurs and thrust them from Pelium to the Aethices.

Apollodorus counts him among the Calydonian hunters, son of Ixion from Larissa, and tells how he and Theseus swore each to marry a daughter of Zeus — Theseus taking the child Helen, Peirithous demanding Persephone herself. In Hades he was seated on the Chair of Forgetfulness and never returned.

Hyginus makes him son of Ixion and brother of Centaurus, a Thessalian, and lists him among the Argonauts. Pausanias saw his battle with the centaurs on the pediment at Athens — Peirithous in the centre, Eurytion seizing his bride, Caeneus and Theseus fighting at his side.
